text: dsh-bash-rtk 是一个 DSH 命令行工具插件，可将符合条件的 Bash 命令交由 rtk（Rust Token Killer）处理以压缩工具输出。它在本地或沙箱 Bash 执行器的 resolve 阶段改写简单命令，只路由白名单中的开发工具；复杂 shell、未知命令或 rtk 不可用时保持原命令。沙箱执行器沿用上游隔离策略，另提供本地执行器。适合希望减少开发命令输出 token 的 DSH 用户。需要自行安装 rtk 并加入 PATH；插件默认禁用，须通过 profile overlay 启用。

dsh-bash-rtk routes eligible simple DSH Bash commands through rtk to shorten tool output. Local and sandbox adapters rewrite commands at resolve; complex shell, unknown tools, or missing rtk pass through unchanged. Install rtk on PATH and enable the overlay; disabled by default.
想让 DSH 跑 git、cargo 这类命令时少返回一些冗长输出。
有没有办法自动压缩 DSH Bash 工具的开发命令结果？
我想让简单的白名单命令自动经过 rtk 处理。
DSH 里执行 npm 或 pytest 时输出太长，怎么精简？
希望保留沙箱 Bash 执行器，同时减少命令输出内容。
DSH 能否在没有 rtk 时自动按原样执行命令？
Route simple developer commands from DSH Bash through rtk to shorten their output.
I need a sandboxed DSH shell that applies rtk filtering to eligible commands.
Can DSH leave pipelines and unknown commands untouched while optimizing common tool output?
Make verbose git, cargo, or test command output more compact in my DSH workflow.
dsh-bash-rtk 的功能「eligible-routing」：符合条件的命令路由：执行器在 resolve 阶段识别白名单首个命令，并在 rtk 可用时加上对应子命令前缀。请求仍由原 Bash 执行器处理。
dsh-bash-rtk 的功能「passthrough」：复杂 shell 与非白名单命令透传：包含管道、重定向等元字符的命令，以及未知程序，都保持原文本，不交给 rtk 改写。
dsh-bash-rtk 的功能「沙箱执行器」：RtkSandboxBashExecutor 替代原沙箱执行器，在 resolve 阶段改写符合条件的命令。
dsh-bash-rtk 的功能「local-executor」：本地执行器：RtkBashExecutor 可替代本地 Bash 执行器，复用其执行规格并仅更新 command 字段。
dsh-bash-rtk 使用前须知：需自行安装 rtk 并让它位于 PATH；启动时探测 rtk --version，若不可用则所有命令按原样透传。（见 src/index.ts:30-39）
dsh-bash-rtk 使用前须知：Cordis overlay 中的执行器默认 disabled，安装本身不会启用功能，需在 profile patch 中切换相关 executor。（见 cordis.patch.yml:4-24）

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Quick Example：The plugin rewrites commands at the `resolve()` boundary — before anything runs:

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Quick Example：| Input (`command`) | Resolved output | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `git status` | `rtk git status` | Simple + whitelisted |
| `cargo build --release` | `rtk cargo build --release` | Simple + whitelisted |
| `git status \| grep x` | `git status \| grep x` | Complex shell — **passthrough** |
| `ls -la` | `ls -la` | Not whitelisted — **passthrough** |
| `git status` (rtk absent) | `git status` | Binary missing — **identity fallback** |
@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Quick Example：Everything else — workdir, timeout, env, exit code, sandbox confinement — is inherited unchanged.

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Requirements：- **Node.js:** >= 20.0.0
- **rtk:** `rtk --version` must exit 0 on PATH (install separately, e.g. `cargo install rtk`)

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Why：LLM agents burn tokens on verbose tool output (`git log`, `cargo build`, `pytest` trails…). `rtk` already knows how to shrink those for 30–90%. This plugin bolts that filtering onto `dsh`'s bash executor so every eligible command is auto-routed through `rtk` — **with zero semantic change** to what actually runs.

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · How it works：```
model → dsh bash tool → RtkBashExecutor.resolve()
                              │
              ┌───────────────┴────────────────┐
         eligible?                         not eligible

Three independent guards decide (see [`src/wrap.ts`](src/wrap.ts)):

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Versioning note：> **Requires:** `rtk` on `PATH` (`rtk --version` exits 0). The plugin does **not** install or manage rtk — **you must install and update rtk yourself** (e.g. `cargo install rtk` or download a release binary). When rtk is absent the plugin is a silent no-op passthrough.
@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Compatibility & version alignment：The plugin is verified against `dsh` **0.2.1-alpha.1** and keeps the `0.1.x` line working.

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Compatibility & version alignment：`dsh` gates the installation of every plugin: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` reads the plugin's
`peerDependencies` and checks each `@deepseek-ai/dsh` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` entry against the
**running `dsh` version** with `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`.
A range whose branches cannot admit `0.2.1-alpha.1` — e.g. the `0.1.1` release's
`… || >=0.1.1-rc.1 <0.2.0-0` — fails that check, and the plugin manager refuses the install with
`is incompatible with dsh 0.2.1-alpha.1` (unless a manual `dsh plugin allow-version` exact-version
exemption is granted). The marketplace applies the same prerelease-aware reading of `engines.dsh`
and the host peers.

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Compatibility & version alignment：The ranges shipped now (see `peerDependencies` in `package.json`) add an explicit `0.2.x` branch:

```
"@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local":   ">=0.0.1-rc.1 <0.1.0 || >=0.1.0-rc.1 <0.1.1 || >=0.1.1-rc.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0"
"@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-sandbox": ">=0.0.1-rc.1 <0.1.0 || >=0.1.0-rc.1 <0.1.1 || >=0.1.1-rc.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0"
"@deepseek-ai/dsh-shell":        ">=0.0.1-rc.1 <0.1.0 || >=0.1.0-rc.1 <0.1.1 || >=0.1.1-rc.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0"
```

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Compatibility & version alignment：The prerelease-branch rule still applies: a broad `>=0.0.1-rc.1 <0.3.0` would *silently* exclude
every `0.1.0-*` / `0.1.1-*` / `0.2.0-*` prerelease under node-semver's default rules (a prerelease
only satisfies a range when some comparator shares its exact `major.minor.patch` tuple *and* also
carries a prerelease tag). Because `dsh`'s gate — and the marketplace — evaluate ranges with
`includePrerelease: true`, those explicit `<0.x.0-0` upper bounds are exactly what admit a running
prerelease such as `0.2.1-alpha.1`.

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Compatibility & version alignment：**What the 0.2 port changed.** The execution seam is unchanged — the plugin still only overrides
`resolve()`, and the 0.2 `ShellExecSpec` merely gains a `sandboxPolicy` field that is spread through
untouched. The compile-time fixes are the module specifier (`cordis` → `@deepseek-ai/cordis`; the
unscoped alias no longer exists) and the executor surface the tests use (`run()`/`start()` were
replaced by `execute()` plus `result()`; `SandboxProvider.confine()` is now async and returns
`Promise<ConfinedArgv>`; `SandboxPolicyService` now requires `ctx.sessionProjections`).

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Compatibility & version alignment：> **Known version skew:** `dsh` (the aggregate, what `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` installs) and its
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` sub-packages are on **separate semver tracks** — the aggregate can be
> `0.1.1-rc.2` while the published sub-packages are still `0.0.1-rc.1`. The ranges above pin to the
> *published* sub-package versions but are checked by `dsh` against its **own** version, so every
> supported release line needs its own explicit branch. Watch the
> [releases](https://github.com/DeepTrial/dsh-bash-rtk/releases) for a matching update.

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · API / Configuration：Both executors accept the same base config as their stock counterparts (`LocalBashExecutor` / `SandboxBashExecutor`) plus one optional field:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rtkAvailable` | `boolean` | `resolveRtk()` result | Force-enable or force-disable rtk wrapping. Useful for tests or deployments where the binary path is non-standard. |

All other options — `cwd`, `timeoutMs`, `graceMs`, etc. — are inherited unchanged from the upstream executors.

@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Which commands are routed：The set of commands eligible for rtk-wrapping is defined by **rtk itself** — see the [rtk command reference](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk#supported-ecosystems) / [`README.md`](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/blob/develop/README.md#test-runners) for the authoritative, maintained list. This plugin mirrors that list; when rtk adds a new subcommand, upgrade rtk (not this plugin) to pick it up.
@deeptrial/dsh-bash-rtk README · Which commands are routed：Complex commands — pipelines, `&&`/`;`, redirects, `$( )`, env assignments — always run natively regardless of the whitelist.
